newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks firm at midday, techs lead way.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks firm at midday, techs lead way.

text.p: U.S. stocks were broadly higher at midday, sparked by a resurgent technology sector which re-assumed leadership of the bull market for the first time in weeks.
The Dow industrials rose 26 points to 6445 and the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite gained 12 to 1270. Nasdaq's move reflected a sharp rally in semiconductor equipment companies.
"The strength seems to be tied to the techs and that would be a good thing," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities.
"We're at a point now where we need to show major firepower to keep the rally going and the techs could provide that leadership," Nie said.

Among the Dow components, International Business Machines Corp remained the standout, climbing 2-3/4 to 156-7/8. The broad rally also pulled in a number of names that had failed to participate in the post-Election Day gains.

Semiconductor equipment maker Applied Materials Inc was the clearest example, surging 5-1/8 to 37-1/8, despite reporting fourth quarter earnings last night that were about half the levels posted a year ago.

However, the company told analysts during a conference call it did not expect the current cyclical downturn it faced would be as severe as those in the past. The disclosure prompted a flurry of upgrades by Wall Street firms, with some raising ratings on Applied Materials' competitors as well.
Among other companies in the sector, KLA Instruments Corp jumped 4-3/4 to 38, Tencor Instruments gained 4-1/4 to 25-1/2 and Lam Research Corp rose 4-7/8 to 34-3/8.
Analysts said the rally came at a key time for the market, which lately has relied on the Dow for its steam.

"It would not be surprising to see some profit-taking in the big stocks," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock and Co. "We're in a rotational market and we're at a point now where fund managers are ferreting through the list of stocks that have been beaten down since July."

Among individual issues, cosmetic company Nu Skin Asia Pacific Inc bounded higher in its New York Stock Exchange debut. Shares jumped 6-1/2 to 29-1/2 on heavy volume in the first trading after Nu Skin's initial public offering. Alrenco Inc tumbled eight points to 11-1/2 after the company warned of weak fourth quarter earnings.
